interactions.summary: Jiang frames Canto 24 as an oral examination Dante must pass before meeting God: Peter, James, and John will test him on faith, hope, and love after Beatrice's teaching is over.
A student reads the canto opening, then Jiang pauses to assign visual homework so the class can register both the poem's imagistic richness and its strangeness.
The student reads Peter's testing of Dante on faith, and Jiang explains the basic paradox: Peter asks for a definition, but Dante answers by quoting Paul's definition from Hebrews.

speaker_notes.note: These segments are quoted canto reading rather than Jiang's own propositions; treat them as setup material for the interpretive claim in seg-0392.

claims.claim: Jiang says Dante's ascent culminates in an oral examination where Peter, James, and John test whether he can define faith, hope, and love well enough to ascend further.
Jiang presents Beatrice's role as completed instruction rather than active assistance: Dante must now demonstrate that he has absorbed heaven's teachings without her help.
Jiang assigns visual-art homework because he wants students to see the Divine Comedy as a highly visual and imaginatively extreme poem rather than a merely textual artifact.
Jiang says the first faith question in Peter's examination is paradoxical because Dante answers by citing Paul's definition from Hebrews rather than producing a purely original definition.

signature_moments.moment: Heaven itself becomes a testing regime: even at the edge of God, Dante still has to sit for an oral exam.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you're in heaven, and they make you take an examination
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures Jiang's comic but serious framing of spiritual ascent as demonstrated understanding rather than mere arrival.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang highlights the weirdness that Peter asks about faith but Dante defers to Paul, as if authority and originality are already in tension inside heaven.
signature_moments.source_phrase: i'm going to refer to the expert on faith which is paul
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This paradox becomes the hinge for Jiang's later claim that Dante subtly revises official doctrine from within.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's frame for Dante's final testing by the apostles before he can ascend to the highest realm.
The scholastic term in the canto for the essential whatness of faith, which Jiang treats as the object of Peter's test.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-17 Jiang shifts from broad civilizational claims about Dante to a close reading of the heaven-side examination on faith, treating Canto 24 as a doctrinal test scene.

uncertainty_notes.note: The quoted canto language is occasionally rough in ASR, so the packet preserves only the stable examination structure and Jiang's explicit interpretation rather than over-normalizing the poetry.
